source.question: Explain motion graphs for JEE from the basics. Cover: x against t graph, tangent slope as velocity, shapes for rest, uniform velocity and uniform acceleration; v against t graph, slope as acceleration, area as displacement, area below the axis negative; distance as total area ignoring signs; a against t graph, area as change in velocity; impossible graphs. Draw one simple diagram: a v against t graph rising from 0 to 20 m/s in 4 s then flat to 10 s, with the area under it shaded. Label only the given values (20 m/s, 4 s, 10 s); say the 160 m area in words, not as a label.

revealGroups.narrationCue: Velocity rises linearly from zero to 20 metres per second at 4 seconds, then stays constant until 10 seconds. The shaded region is the area under the graph.

teachingTimeline.narration: On a position–time graph, tangent slope gives velocity: rest is horizontal, uniform velocity is a straight line, and uniform acceleration gives a parabola. On a velocity–time graph, slope gives acceleration. Here the rising phase has an acceleration of five metres per second squared, and the flat phase has zero acceleration.

Calculate the shaded triangle and rectangle after reading the setup. Their combined area gives a displacement of one hundred sixty metres. Because velocity is never negative here, the distance is also one hundred sixty metres. In general, area below the time axis counts negatively toward displacement; distance adds the magnitudes of all areas.

Signed area under an acceleration–time graph gives the change in velocity. A vertical segment in a position–time or velocity–time graph would assign multiple values to one time, so it cannot represent single-valued motion. For ordinary finite velocity or acceleration, respectively, those graphs also cannot have a vertical tangent.

teachingTimeline.narration: A motion graph plots a quantity against time. On a position–time graph, a secant slope gives average velocity and a tangent slope gives instantaneous velocity. A horizontal line means rest; a straight sloping line means uniform velocity; a parabolic curve represents uniform nonzero acceleration.

On a velocity–time graph, slope gives acceleration. Here the rise from zero to twenty metres per second in four seconds gives an acceleration of five metres per second squared. The flat portion has zero acceleration.

Signed area under a velocity–time graph gives displacement. The triangle contributes forty metres and the rectangle contributes one hundred and twenty metres, for a displacement of one hundred and sixty metres. Because velocity is never negative here, the distance is also one hundred and sixty metres. In general, area below the time axis contributes negatively to displacement, while distance adds area magnitudes without cancelling signs.

On an acceleration–time graph, signed area gives the change in velocity. A graph assigning more than one position, velocity, or acceleration to the same time is impossible as a graph of that quantity against time; a vertical velocity–time segment fails this test.

source.question: Explain motion graphs for JEE from the basics. annotations.text: From 0 to 4 s the straight rising line means uniform acceleration: its slope is the acceleration. From 4 s to 10 s the flat line means constant velocity 20 m/s, so zero acceleration.

The area under this v-t graph is the displacement: a triangle of base 4 s and height 20 m/s giving 40 m, plus a rectangle of width 6 s and height 20 m/s giving 120 m, totalling 160 m. Since v is never negative, distance equals displacement here.
On an x-t graph the tangent slope at any instant is the velocity: horizontal means rest, a straight sloped line means uniform velocity, and a parabola means uniform acceleration.
On an a-t graph the area under the curve is the change in velocity over that interval.

Impossible graphs: a vertical x-t or v-t segment (two positions or velocities at one time), a body at two places at one instant, or a v-t graph with infinite slope implying infinite acceleration. Graphs must be single-valued functions of t with finite slope.

teachingTimeline.narration: Draw the velocity-time axes: v in m/s vertically, t in s horizontally.
Plot the motion: a straight line from (0,0) to (4,20) while the car speeds up, then horizontal from (4,20) to (10,20) at steady speed.
The slope of the rising part is Δv/Δt = (20−0)/4 = 5 m/s², the acceleration.
The flat part has zero slope, so acceleration is zero and velocity stays 20 m/s.
The area under the graph gives distance: triangle ½×4×20 = 40 m plus rectangle 20×6 = 120 m, total 160 m.
